tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative-ish framing ('Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed...'), lists many explicit trigger contexts (ModelError, 5xx, cold-starts, throttling, async backlog, batch transform failures, right-sizing questions), and focuses on user-observable symptoms rather than internal implementation. It is a dense paragraph but stays within a reasonable length for the scope covered (four areas), and clearly delineates scope boundaries (diagnoses the endpoint, not provider/infra fault locus).
tests.evidence: "Diagnose Amazon SageMaker inference that fails, errors, is slow, scales wrong or costs too much... Use this skill when an endpoint is Failed or never passes its health check... when a serverless endpoint cold-starts or throttles; when async requests never notify, back up or fail on large inputs; when a transform job fails to parse records..."

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific — check-ids, API calls, router table, quirks, catalog mappings. It doesn't explain generic concepts like what SageMaker or VPC is; it jumps straight into specific procedures and non-obvious facts.
tests.evidence: Load checks-sagemaker-inference.md before writing any finding: it holds the full detection rules, remediations, and citations.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps detailed reference data (full check catalog details, metric thresholds, API field lists) in references/ files and only embeds a compact index table and router table in SKILL.md, which is appropriately scoped rather than a large reference dump.

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, high-stakes operations (read-only guardrails, severity assignment, evidence rules) are given exact, non-negotiable instructions, while judgment-heavy areas (fit decision between batch/async/serverless, right-sizing) are explained with reasoning rather than rigid steps.
tests.evidence: Never invent a threshold... a tuning/right-sizing judgment with no AWS-published number is marked workload-specific... Report the fit with the observed config and metric values.

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple inference deployment options exist (real-time/serverless/async/batch), the skill gives decision criteria and a clear default path per scenario rather than listing them as undifferentiated equal choices.
tests.evidence: Low or bursty traffic on an always-on real-time endpoint is the idle-cost signal LLM-SM-008. Whether that traffic belongs on serverless... or async... is LLM-SM-SERVE-005, driven by payload size and invocation duration.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic procedure (identify area, read config, check scaling, check metrics, assemble findings) applicable to any endpoint/job, not a one-off instance-specific task.
tests.evidence: Run the steps in order and track progress against this checklist... Step 1: Identify the area and enumerate resources.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has an explicit 'Common wrong answers' and 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious API behaviors and misleading signals, functioning as a gotchas section.
tests.evidence: "The endpoint is `InService`, so it's serving traffic and the queue is fine." `InService` is control-plane state; a real-time, async or serverless variant can be `InService` with `CurrentInstanceCount` = 0...
